description:
About the Position

Leiden University's Centre for Linguistics invites applications for a PhD candidate working on Dutch morphology and constructicography. The project develops computational descriptions of Dutch word formation and construction patterns, contributing to digital language resources that connect morphological analysis with construction-based lexicography.

The candidate will build and analyse morphological datasets for Dutch, develop formal and computational models of word structure, and integrate findings into constructicographic resources that describe how constructions carry meaning. The work sits between theoretical linguistics and computational lexicography, with outputs including publications and openly available language resources.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a research master's in linguistics, computational linguistics or a neighbouring field, with demonstrable affinity for morphology and data-driven language research. Programming skills for corpus and database work are expected. The position is a salaried four-year PhD track under the CAO-NU collective agreement; given the project's focus on Dutch, a strong command of Dutch is required, and the daily working language of the centre is English.

Highlights

  • Computational morphology of Dutch
  • Constructicography and construction-based lexicography
  • Morphological datasets and language resources
  • Formal modelling of word formation
  • Corpus and database methods
  • Salaried four-year PhD under the CAO-NU agreement

About Leiden University

Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and a member of the League of European Research Universities (LERU). Its seven faculties in Leiden and The Hague cover humanities, law, social and behavioural sciences, medicine, science, archaeology and governance. Doctoral candidates at Leiden are salaried employees under the CAO-NU collective agreement rather than fee-paying students, which makes its PhD positions fully funded by design. All academic vacancies, including PhD and postdoctoral roles, are advertised on the university's dedicated careers portal.
